Add, beside withQuery, and export from the package entry src/index.ts a function filterQuery(input: string, predicate: (key: string, value: string | string[]) => boolean): string that returns input keeping only the query parameters for which predicate returns true. Its rules: an input that contains no "?" is returned exactly as given (filterQuery("file:///C:/x", () => false) is "file:///C:/x", not normalized). Otherwise predicate is called once for each key of getQuery(input), in that order, with the decoded key and the value getQuery gives it (a string, or an array of strings for a repeated key, so a repeated key is kept or dropped as a whole), and the URL is rebuilt the way withQuery rebuilds it: filterQuery(input, () => true) equals withQuery(input, {}) for every input that contains "?"; protocol, auth, host, path and fragment are kept as withQuery keeps them; the kept parameters are encoded as withQuery encodes them; and the "?" is left out when no parameter remains. svgo's removeScripts plugin (plugins/removeScripts.js) removes scripting from an SVG: script elements, event attributes, executable attributes of HTML inside foreignObject, and links with an executable URL. A link is an <a> element whose href or *:href attribute is a javascript: or vbscript: URL, or a data: URL of an HTML, XHTML or SVG document; the plugin replaces such an element by its element children (its text children are dropped). Whether a URL is executable is decided by isExecutableUrl in lib/svgo/tools.js, which hasScripts in the same file also uses, so other plugins (cleanupIds, minifyStyles, removeHiddenElems, removeUselessStrokeAndFill) leave documents with executable links alone. Two kinds of executable link survive today. First, an SVG anchor written with a namespace prefix: in <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:svg="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><svg:a xlink:href="javascript:alert(1)"><rect width="1"/></svg:a></svg> the svg:a element is kept with its link, although it is an SVG <a>. Second, a URL whose scheme is split by ASCII tab, line feed or carriage return characters, such as href="java	script:alert(1)": browsers remove those characters from a URL before parsing it, so the link runs, but isExecutableUrl does not recognise it. Its rules: an input that contains no "?" is returned exactly as given (filterQuery("file:///C:/x", () => false) is "file:///C:/x", not normalized). p-limit's limitFunction(function_, options) in index.js returns a function that runs function_ with limited concurrency, and its options accept rejectOnClear just as pLimit's do, but the returned function offers no way to discard the calls still waiting to run, so that option has no effect there. Today limitFunction(async () => 'done', {concurrency: 1}).clearQueue is undefined, and calling it throws "TypeError: limited.clearQueue is not a function". Give the returned function a clearQueue() method that discards the calls that have not started yet, exactly as clearQueue() does for a pLimit limiter: it returns undefined; calls already running are not cancelled and settle as usual; the function of a discarded call is never invoked; with rejectOnClear: true each discarded call's promise rejects with an error whose name is "AbortError", and without it (the default) the discarded promises stay unsettled; calls made after clearing run normally, and calls that are still running keep counting against the concurrency limit. For example, with const limited = limitFunction(async x => { await delay(40); return x * 2; }, {concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: true}), calling limited(1), limited(2) and limited(3) and then limited.clearQueue() gives 2 for the first call and AbortError rejections for the other two, whose function never runs. Clearing one limited function does not affect another one, even when both were made with the same options object, and clearQueue() on a limited function with nothing waiting is harmless. The TypeScript declarations in index.d.ts must describe the method: for const lf = limitFunction(async (_a: string) => 'ok', {concurrency: 1}), lf.clearQueue() must type-check with type void, and lf('input') must stay Promise<string>.
